title: In Gladiator (2000) how did the Praetorian Guard reach Maximus’s family before him?

commenti.body:
For the same reason the Marcus Aurelius didn't tell a single soul except Maximus about his plans for Rome's government before he was murdered: because then there'd be no movie.

I hate that's the answer because it's always deeply unsatisfying, and in a more True Film-style discussion it opens the conversation of whether it's bad writing, or necessary writing, but the murder of Maximus's family is most of narrative thrust of the film and how it happened isn't really important. Like, Ridley Scott and whoever else was writing the film probably didn't sit down and think "well, a man on a mission could probably outpace a caravan, let's construct a scene to show why that didn't happen", they just assumed the audience would know he was beaten in the race. That, or the whole "take him out into the woods" thing was sufficient.

Unless there are interviews or film notes otherwise, anything beyond that is just conjecture. Maybe they had messengers running all over at top speed and one of them happened to bring the orders to soldiers closer to Maximus's home? We'd have to go digging into non-movies sources of Roman message systems which, given that 90% of the movie isn't based in historical accuracy anyway seems like an exercise in futility.

I'm personally more bothered by the Marcus Aurelius thing, it seemed so much more preventable even within the movie's logic. Still one of my favorite films of all time, though.

One thing to also note is that a lot of footage is often left on the cutting room floor too. There may have even been a scene that was just cut for length. It happens all the time with film continuity errors.

I don't mind the occasional improbability. But improbabilities within probabilities will kill an otherwise great movie. I had this problem with Collateral, which is very similar to what you're describing: the police are trying to get to a club before Tom Cruise's character does, which they have to do because the guy they're trying to save didn't answer the phone. As if they don't have any other number they could call, including nearby police or FBI. Then, they race down there, but don't make it in time. Then there's a shootout and Tom Cruise escapes from the club by teleporting onto the street.

The Praetorians probably did have the ability to change horses at pre-assigned stations along the way. Even with two horses, Maximus can't go full out all the way across Europe the way Praetorians on official Imperial business can.

According to [this source](https://www.historyofinformation.com/detail.php?entryid=3961) carrier pigeons were used before that time. They would have been faster, and able to relay the orders before Maximus reach his home.

It also didn't show necessary stops, sleeping etc. With his wound, he likely would pass out and oversleep on occasion. Despite how it's shot, I don't think we are meant to think *he didn't stop or sleep at all*.
It shows him stop at night with a camp fire
Damn I had no idea they used carrier pigeons way back then, I only see them referenced in ww1, TIL
